record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Which sporadic finite simple groups occur as automorphism groups of chiral d-polytopes?

evidence.quote: Problem 2 Determine which sporadic finite simple groups are automorphism groups of chiral d-polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $d$ is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ (with a minimum and a maximum element) whose elements are called faces, equipped with a rank function with values in $\{-1,0,1,\dots,d\}$, satisfying the standard axioms: every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly $d+2$ faces (one of each rank), $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds (for each $i\in\{0,\dots,d-1\}$, given a flag, there is exactly one other flag differing only in its rank-$i$ face). The automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{P})$ is the group of order-preserving bijections of $\mathcal{P}$ to itself; it acts freely on the set of flags. The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called chiral if $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{P})$ has exactly two orbits on flags such that any two adjacent flags lie in distinct orbits.

Recall that the sporadic finite simple groups are the 26 finite simple groups not belonging to one of the infinite families (cyclic of prime order, alternating $A_n$ for $n\ge 5$, or finite simple groups of Lie type): namely $M_{11}, M_{12}, M_{22}, M_{23}, M_{24}, J_1, J_2, J_3, J_4, Co_1, Co_2, Co_3, Fi_{22}, Fi_{23}, Fi_{24}', HS, McL, He, Ru, Suz, O'N, HN, Ly, Th, B,$ and $M$ (the Monster).

Determine, for each sporadic finite simple group $G$ and each integer $d\ge 3$, whether there exists a chiral abstract $d$-polytope $\mathcal{P}$ with $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{P}) \cong G$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known via computational atlases of chiral polytopes for small almost simple groups (Hartley–Hubard–Leemans) and case-by-case studies for individual sporadic groups (e.g. Mathieu, Higman–Sims, Held, O'Nan, Conway groups), but a complete classification across all 26 sporadic groups and all ranks $d$ does not appear to be available; the problem remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Atlas of Chiral Polytopes for Small Almost Simple Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Atlas of chiral polytopes whose automorphism group is an almost simple group from the ATLAS of Finite Groups.
status_evidence.claim: Computational enumerations of chiral polytopes have been carried out for small almost simple groups, including several sporadic groups, but not for all sporadic groups.

status_evidence.title: Polytopes Derived from Sporadic Simple Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Highest ranked polytopes from sporadic groups studied include rank 5 polytopes from Higman-Sims and M24; sporadic groups up to the Held group analyzed.
status_evidence.claim: Only sporadic groups up to a certain order have been systematically analyzed, leaving the larger sporadic groups (including the Monster) unresolved.
